title: Let the Feeling Finish Its Sentence
core_idea: Accepting an emotion instead of arguing with it lets it move and pass in its own time.
text: Sadness arrives, and almost at once we start arguing with it. I shouldn't feel this. I should be over it by now. But a feeling that is pushed away often just waits by the door. Acceptance can be as simple as letting an emotion finish its sentence. Noticing where it sits in the body. Naming it softly. Sadness. Worry. Disappointment. You don't have to like it, and you don't have to act on it. You're only allowing it to be here for a while, the way you'd let a tired friend sit down. Many people find that feelings move more freely once they are no longer resisted. They rise, they speak, and in their own time, they pass.
description: A gentle practice of accepting a difficult feeling instead of fighting it, so it can move and pass in its own time.
